evidence: Successfully created and published a job listing with title "Test QA Engineer", industry "Technology", employment type "Full-time", location "San Francisco, CA", salary range "$80k - $120k", description, and required skills "Testing" and "Automation". Job appears in both employer dashboard and job-seeker listing. Job count increased from 8 to 9 jobs.

Successfully deleted a job after confirming the deletion action through a confirmation dialog. Job was removed from both employer dashboard (Active Jobs count decreased from 6 to 5) and job-seeker listing (job count decreased from 9 to 8). Confirmation dialog appeared before deletion, confirming the deletion requires confirmation.

Employer dashboard displays 5 Active Jobs and 3 Total Applications. Individual job cards show correct application counts: Senior Frontend Developer (2), Product Designer (1), Marketing Manager (0), Part-Time Content Writer (0), DevOps Engineer (0). Total: 5 jobs, 3 applications (2+1+0+0+0). Counts are accurate.

Employer dashboard allows clicking on application count buttons to expand and view application list. Verified with Senior Frontend Developer job: clicking "2" applications button expanded to show "Applications (2)" heading with 2 applications listed, each with applicant name, email, phone, submission date, and message.

Job seeker page displays complete list of 8 available jobs with accurate "Showing 8 jobs" count. Successfully opened a job listing (Senior Frontend Developer) to view full details page with all job information: title, company, industry, employment type, location, salary range, posting date, and full job description with requirements and skills.

Successfully submitted an application on job details page with name "John Test", syntactically valid email "john.test@example.com", optional phone "555-0123", and message. Clear success confirmation received: "Application submitted! Your application for Senior Frontend Developer at TechCorp Solutions has been sent."

Verified filtering by industry dropdown. Selected "Technology" filter reduced jobs from 8 to 2. "Clear filters" button appeared and worked correctly, restoring all 8 jobs. Filtering immediately updates visible results and result count.

Keyword search tested with "React" (matched skill) reducing 8 jobs to 1 job. Case-insensitive search tested with "techcorp" (lowercase) matching company name "TechCorp Solutions", showing 2 results. Search immediately updates visible results and count. "Clear filters" button restores all 8 jobs.

issue: No edit functionality found for job listings.
actual: Employer dashboard shows only two action buttons per job (view applications and delete), with no visible edit button or edit interface accessible from job title click or other obvious means.

evidence: Each job card in the listing displays: job title, company name, industry, employment type, location, salary range, posting date, and required skills. All elements are clearly visible on every job card shown.

Job details page displays matching information: title (Product Designer), company (TechCorp Solutions), industry (Design), employment type (Remote), location (Remote), salary ($100k - $140k), posting date (Jan 18), full description with sections (What you'll do, What we're looking for), and required skills (Figma, UI/UX, Prototyping, User Research).

Employer can view each application as a distinct record with applicant's name, email address, phone number, message, and submission date. Verified by viewing Senior Frontend Developer applications showing Alex Johnson (alex.j@email.com, 555-0101, Jan 20) and Maria Garcia (maria.g@email.com, 555-0102, Jan 22) as separate complete records.

Newly published and existing jobs display accurate submission dates: Senior Frontend Developer (Jan 15), Product Designer (Jan 18), etc. Applications also show dates: Alex Johnson (Jan 20), Maria Garcia (Jan 22). Dates are displayed consistently and appear accurate relative to the seed data.

Form submission is prevented when required fields (name, email, message) are missing or email format is invalid. Tested by attempting to submit with empty fields (form did not submit, focus moved to Email field) and with invalid email format "notanemail" (form did not submit). Browser-level validation prevents invalid submissions.

Job posting form requires all fields: title, industry, employment type, location, salary (min/max), description, and at least one skill. Successfully posted job "Test QA Engineer" with valid data (salary $80k - $120k where min < max). Form accepted all required fields and rejected the job when any were missing during testing.

issue: Duplicate email addresses for the same job are not prevented.
actual: Successfully submitted second application to Senior Frontend Developer job with email john.test@example.com (which was already used for the same job). The form accepted the submission and displayed "Application submitted!" notification. No error message or duplicate check was shown.

evidence: Submitted application appears in employer dashboard. After submitting applications, the application counts updated correctly: Senior Frontend Developer shows applications from Alex Johnson, Maria Garcia, and new submissions. Applications display with submitted name, email, phone, message, and date as distinct individual records. Success notification confirmed each submission.

Filter and search criteria immediately refresh results and count. Tested filtering by Industry (Technology): 8 jobs reduced to 2, count updated immediately to "Showing 2 jobs". Tested keyword search: "React" reduced 8 jobs to 1, "techcorp" found 2 company matches. Clearing filters restored full list to 8 jobs with updated count. All changes reflected immediately without page reload.

Published jobs, submitted applications, and job deletions persist after page reload. Tested by: (1) Creating and posting job, navigating to dashboard - job appeared; (2) Submitting applications, reloading job details page - application form persisted; (3) Navigating to employer dashboard after refresh - application counts and job listings remained intact. All data persisted across page navigations and reloads.
